Moving Averages – This method takes several past data points and then calculates the average of those data points, this can smooth out price fluctuations. The score for this method is 3 out of 10, meaning there is a higher probability the stock will continue to go down in price.

MACD (Moving Average Convergence Divergence) – The MACD takes the difference between two exponential moving averages to measure the relationship between the moving averages. The score for this method is 2 out of 10, meaning there is a significant chance the stock value will go down in the future.

Relative Strength Index (RSI) – The RSI measures the magnitude of recent price changes to evaluate overbought or oversold conditions in the price of a stock. The score for this method is 5 out of 10, meaning there is an even change that price will move in either direction.

Fibonacci Retracement – Fibonacci retracement levels are calculated by taking two significant price points and dividing the vertical distance between them into key Fibonacci ratios. The score for this method is 1 out of 10, meaning there is a strong chance the stock will continue to decrease in value.

Bollinger Bands – Bollinger Bands are a type of technical analysis that helps traders to identify the price action in relation to its historical volatility. The score for this method is 8 out of 10, meaning there is a good chance the stock will increase in price.
